clean_source_blocks.text: Emergency response has rescued 67 people, including 15 children, from one of the country’s worst maritime disasters A ferry carrying 116 passengers and crew sank ⁠off the coast of Guyana in South America ⁠late Saturday, with 67 ⁠people, ​including 15 children, rescued so far, according to Guyana ⁠authorities. A massive search-and-rescue operation continues for dozens of missing passengers in what has been described by officials as one of the country’s worst maritime disasters. Continue reading...

Emergency response has rescued 67 people, including 15 children, from one of the country’s worst maritime disasters A ferry carrying 116 passengers and crew sank ⁠off the coast of Guyana in South America ⁠late Saturday, with 67 ⁠people, ​including 15 children, rescued so far, according to Guyana ⁠authorities. A massive search-and-rescue operation continues for dozens of missing passengers in what has been described by officials as one of the country’s worst maritime disasters. The ferry MV Barima left Georgetown, the capital of the English-speaking South American country, on Saturday at about 3.15pm for Port Kaituma, located in the oil-rich Essequibo region and just off the border with Venezuela. A distress call was received shortly after 11pm, prompting an emergency response involving the Guyana Defence Force Coast Guard and Air Corps, private aircraft, fishing vessels and civilian volunteers.

Emergency crews launch search efforts after a ferry sinks near Guyana, with dozens of passengers feared missing A massive search and rescue operation is underway off the North Atlantic coast of Guyana after a passenger ferry capsized late Saturday night, leaving dozens of people missing. The ferry was traveling from Guyana’s capital city, Georgetown, to the northwest village of Port Kaituma when it capsized near Iron Punt and the Pomeroon River. The vessel, MV Barima, was carrying 116 passengers and 17 crew members when it encountered distress at approximately 11:00 p.m. local time on Saturday, July 18. As reported 67 people including 15 children and several crew members, have been successfully rescued till Sunday. Medical teams have been dispatched to the area to treat survivors as they are brought ashore.

The Guyana Coast Guard, Defence Force, and several local private vessels are actively scouring the waters for the remaining passengers who are still unaccounted for. As reported by Al Jazeera, Public Works Minister, Juan Edghill, noted that the ferry was heavily equipped with safety gear before departure, including 250 life jackets, two rigid life rafts, and six inflatable life rafts. Guyana's Prime Minister, Mark Phillips, stated that search operations will continue until every effort has been made to find survivors While a formal investigation will officially launch once the rescue phase is over, preliminary reports suggest that the vessel did not strike an object, instead early accounts from survivors indicate that the vessel was hit and overwhelmed by a massive wave.

Emergency response has rescued 67 people, including 15 children, from one of the country’s worst maritime disasters

A ferry carrying 116 passengers and crew sank ⁠off the coast of Guyana in South America ⁠late Saturday, with 67 ⁠people, ​including 15 children, rescued so far, according to Guyana ⁠authorities.

A massive search-and-rescue operation continues for dozens of missing passengers in what has been described by officials as one of the country’s worst maritime disasters.

The ferry MV Barima left Georgetown, the capital of the English-speaking South American country, on Saturday at about 3.15pm for Port Kaituma, located in the oil-rich Essequibo region and just off the border with Venezuela.

A distress call was received shortly after 11pm, prompting an emergency response involving the Guyana Defence Force Coast Guard and Air Corps, private aircraft, fishing vessels and civilian volunteers.

Juan Edghill, the minister of public works, said preliminary investigations indicate the vessel was operating within its legal limits.

“There was no engine problem or any mechanical problem. It had nothing to do with overload. It had to do with the tide,” Edghill told local reporters.

He said the MV Barima was certified to carry 397 passengers and 284 tonnes of cargo. Its manifest showed it was transporting 268 tonnes of cargo, below its authorised capacity.

The ship was equipped with 250 lifejackets, two lifeboats and six inflatable rafts, Edghill said.

In a statement on Sunday, Guyana’s prime minister, Mark Phillips, said the search and rescue coordination centre had expanded the search area from 400 sq km to 1,070 sq km, with additional aircraft and vessels deployed alongside local fisherfolk familiar with the waters.

The 67 survivors include 41 men, 11 women and 15 children.

As the rescue effort continues, survivors recounted the moments when the ferry overturned in darkness.

Adam Matabheek, who was travelling with his wife, brother, sister-in-law and three young nieces and nephews, said he noticed the vessel leaning several hours before it capsized.

“We dismissed it as rough water and went to sleep,” he said.

“I ended up in the water,” he recalled, saying he managed to grab a lifejacket before drifting through the night.

His wife, Carlita Matabheek, who cannot swim, said she became trapped inside the overturned vessel before a lifejacket fell within her reach.

A massive search and rescue operation is underway off the North Atlantic coast of Guyana after a passenger ferry capsized late Saturday night, leaving dozens of people missing.

The ferry was traveling from Guyana’s capital city, Georgetown, to the northwest village of Port Kaituma when it capsized near Iron Punt and the Pomeroon River.

The vessel, MV Barima, was carrying 116 passengers and 17 crew members when it encountered distress at approximately 11:00 p.m. local time on Saturday, July 18.

As reported 67 people including 15 children and several crew members, have been successfully rescued till Sunday.

Medical teams have been dispatched to the area to treat survivors as they are brought ashore.

payload.title: Kymmeniä kateissa matkustajalautan upottua Guyanan edustalla
payload.summary: Ainakin 67 ihmistä on pelastettu MV Barima -lautan upottua Guyanan edustalla. Kymmeniä ihmisiä on edelleen kateissa, ja laaja etsintäoperaatio jatkuu.
payload.content:
Guyanan edustalla Pohjois-Atlantilla tapahtuneessa lauttaonnettomuudessa on pelastettu ainakin 67 ihmistä, joista 15 on lapsia. MV Barima -matkustajalautta kaatui ja upposi myöhään lauantai-iltana matkalla Georgetownista Port Kaitumaan. Kymmeniä ihmisiä on edelleen kateissa, ja viranomaiset jatkavat laajaa etsintä- ja pelastusoperaatiota.

## Etsintöihin osallistuu aluksia ja lentokoneita

MV Barima lähti Guyanan pääkaupungista Georgetownista lauantaina 18. heinäkuuta noin kello 15.15 kohti maan luoteisosassa sijaitsevaa Port Kaitumaa. Kohde sijaitsee öljyvaroiltaan merkittävällä Essequibon alueella lähellä Venezuelan rajaa. Aluksella oli yli sata matkustajaa ja miehistön jäsentä. Hätäkutsu vastaanotettiin hieman kello 23:n jälkeen, kun lautta oli Iron Puntin ja Pomeroonjoen lähistöllä.

Hätäkutsu käynnisti pelastustoimet, joihin osallistuvat Guyanan puolustusvoimien rannikkovartiosto ja ilmajoukot, yksityiset lentokoneet, kalastusalukset sekä siviilivapaaehtoiset. Alukset ja ilma-alukset etsivät yhä matkustajia ja miehistön jäseniä, joiden olinpaikka ei ole tiedossa. Paikalle on lähetetty myös lääkintäryhmiä hoitamaan maihin tuotuja selviytyjiä.

Sunnuntaihin mennessä pelastettujen joukossa oli 15 lasta ja useita miehistön jäseniä. Viranomaiset ovat kuvanneet tapahtunutta yhdeksi Guyanan vakavimmista merionnettomuuksista. Pääministeri Mark Phillipsin mukaan etsintää jatketaan, kunnes kaikki mahdollinen on tehty eloonjääneiden löytämiseksi.

## Onnettomuuden syy tutkitaan myöhemmin

Onnettomuuden syytä ei ole vahvistettu. Alustavien tietojen mukaan alus ei törmännyt esteeseen tai muuhun kohteeseen. Selviytyjien ensimmäisten kertomusten perusteella suuri aalto iski lauttaan ja sai sen valtaansa. Viranomaiset eivät ole vielä esittäneet lopullista arviota tapahtumien kulusta.

Guyanan julkisten töiden ministeri Juan Edghill on kertonut, että lautta oli ennen lähtöä varustettu 250 pelastusliivillä, kahdella jäykkärunkoisella pelastuslautalla ja kuudella ilmatäytteisellä pelastuslautalla.

Virallinen tutkinta käynnistetään vasta pelastusvaiheen päätyttyä. Siihen asti viranomaisten ensisijaisena tehtävänä on löytää kateissa olevat ja tuoda pelastetut hoitoon. Etsintä jatkui sunnuntaina rannikkovartioston, puolustusvoimien ja paikallisten alusten voimin.
summary_bullets: Ainakin 67 ihmistä, heidän joukossaan 15 lasta, on pelastettu.
Kymmeniä MV Barimalla olleita ihmisiä on edelleen kateissa.
Onnettomuuden syy vahvistetaan vasta pelastusvaiheen jälkeen tehtävässä tutkinnassa.

As reported by Al Jazeera, Public Works Minister, Juan Edghill, noted that the ferry was heavily equipped with safety gear before departure, including 250 life jackets, two rigid life rafts, and six inflatable life rafts. Guyana's Prime Minister, Mark Phillips, stated that search operations will continue until every effort has been made to find survivors While a formal investigation will officially launch once the rescue phase is over, preliminary reports suggest that the vessel did not strike an object, instead early accounts from survivors indicate that the vessel was hit and overwhelmed by a massive wave.
